Detailed Description

Linear chained hashtable.

This hashtable resizes dynamically and progressively using a variation of the linear hashing algorithm described in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_hashing

It starts with the minimal size of 64 buckets, it doubles the size when it reaches a load factor greater than 0.5, and it halves the size when the load factor is lower than 0.125.

The progressive resize spreads resizing work across insert and delete operations, reducing pauses caused by resizing the entire table at once. Resizing may traverse a whole bucket, so many collisions can still make an individual operation expensive.

For resizing, a dynamic array that supports access to non-contiguous segments is used. In this way, we only allocate additional table segments on the heap, without freeing the previous table, and thus not increasing the heap fragmentation.

The resize takes place inside tommy_hashlin_insert() and tommy_hashlin_remove(). No resize is done in the tommy_hashlin_search() operation.

To initialize the hashtable you have to call tommy_hashlin_init().

tommy_hashlin hashlin;
tommy_hashlin_init(&hashlin);

Initializes the hashtable.

To insert elements in the hashtable you have to call tommy_hashlin_insert() for each element. In the insertion call you have to specify the address of the node, the address of the element, and the hash value of the key to use. The address of the element is used to initialize the tommy_node::data field of the node, and the hash to initialize the tommy_node::index field.

struct element {
int value;
// other fields
tommy_node node;
};
struct element* elem = malloc(sizeof(struct element)); // creates the element
elem->value = ...; // initializes the element
tommy_hashlin_insert(&hashlin, &elem->node, elem, tommy_inthash_u32(elem->value)); // inserts the element

To find an element in the hashtable you have to call tommy_hashlin_search() providing a comparison function, its argument, and the hash of the key to search.

int compare(const void* arg, const void* elem)
{
return *(const int*)arg != ((const struct element*)elem)->value;
}
int value_to_find = 1;
struct element* elem = tommy_hashlin_search(&hashlin, compare, &value_to_find, tommy_inthash_u32(value_to_find));
if (!elem) {
// not found
} else {
// found
}

To iterate over all the elements in the hashtable with the same key, you have to use tommy_hashlin_bucket() and follow the tommy_node::next pointer until 0. You have also to check explicitly for the key, as the bucket may contain different keys.

int value_to_find = 1;
tommy_node* i = tommy_hashlin_bucket(&hashlin, tommy_inthash_u32(value_to_find));
while (i) {
struct element* elem = i->data; // gets the element pointer
if (elem->value == value_to_find) {
printf("%d\n", elem->value); // process the element
}
i = i->next; // goes to the next element
}

To remove an element from the hashtable you have to call tommy_hashlin_remove() providing a comparison function, its argument, and the hash of the key to search and remove.

struct element* elem = tommy_hashlin_remove(&hashlin, compare, &value_to_remove, tommy_inthash_u32(value_to_remove));
if (elem) {
free(elem); // frees the element allocated memory
}

To destroy the hashtable you have to deinitialize it calling tommy_hashlin_done(). Elements can still be contained when calling this function, but their memory is not freed by it and must be managed separately (for example, freed with tommy_hashlin_foreach()).

tommy_hashlin_done(&hashlin);
tommy_hashlin_done
TOMMY_API void tommy_hashlin_done(tommy_hashlin *hashlin)
Deinitializes the hashtable.

If you need to iterate over all the elements in the hashtable, you can use tommy_hashlin_foreach() or tommy_hashlin_foreach_arg(). For traversal that permits insertions and removals, use tommy_hashlin_head() and tommy_hashlin_next(), or tommy_hashlin_tail() and tommy_hashlin_prev(). Hashes are compared from the least significant bit to the most significant bit, with 0 before 1. Equal hashes are visited in insertion order. This order is independent of the number of buckets and progressive resizing. It differs from the bucket order used by foreach and to_list.

Iterators are pointers to nodes currently contained in the hashtable. Inserting elements or removing other nodes does not invalidate them or change the relative iteration order of the remaining elements. A forward or backward traversal visits every original element that remains contained, even if removals cause buckets to merge or insertions split them. New elements can be visited if inserted after the current position in the traversal direction; elements inserted before it need not be visited.

Removing the pointed node invalidates its use as an iterator, even if its storage has not been freed. Obtain the next or previous node before removal, and keep that saved node contained until continuing the traversal.

tommy_hashlin_node* i = tommy_hashlin_head(&hashlin);
while (i) {
tommy_hashlin_node* next = tommy_hashlin_next(&hashlin, i);
if (should_remove(i->data)) {
free(tommy_hashlin_remove_existing(&hashlin, i));
}
i = next;
}

Changing a hash with tommy_hashlin_rehash_existing() can change iteration order, so the traversal guarantee does not cover rehashing during traversal. After swapping containers, use the container that now contains the node. Clearing or deinitializing the container invalidates all its iterators. Concurrent traversal and modification require external synchronization.

Iterator calls scan bucket contents without allocating or modifying memory. With a good hash function and the table's low load factor, a full traversal runs in expected linear O(n) time. In pathological cases with severe hash collisions, traversal degrades to quadratic O(n^2) time. Use foreach for guaranteed linear traversal when no insertions or removals are needed.

◆ tommy_hashlin_swap()

void tommy_hashlin_swap ( tommy_hashlin *  first,
tommy_hashlin *  second 
)

Exchanges the complete state of two initialized hashtables, including bucket allocations and progressive resize state.

The hashtables must not share nodes. Nodes and elements are not accessed or modified. Existing node pointers remain valid and belong to the other hashtable. Passing the same hashtable twice has no effect. Both hashtables remain usable and deinitializable.

Parameters
firstThe first hashtable.
secondThe second hashtable.
Note
This operation is O(1) with respect to the number of elements.

◆ tommy_hashlin_clear()

TOMMY_API void tommy_hashlin_clear ( tommy_hashlin *  hashlin)

Removes all elements and resets the hashtable to its initial state.

As after tommy_hashlin_init(), it can be reused immediately. Resetting the hashtable is intentional. Keeping a large empty table would make subsequent removals expensive, as progressive shrinking could require scanning many empty buckets. Any pending resize is canceled. No new memory is allocated. Elements are not freed and nodes are not accessed or modified. Their links must not be used to traverse the previous contents. You can call this function after tommy_hashlin_foreach() has freed the elements. Subsequent insertions and removals retain the normal resizing policy.

Parameters
hashlinThe hashtable.
Note
This operation is O(m + log b), where m is the initial number of buckets and b is the number of allocated buckets before the call. Nodes are not traversed.

Inserts an element only if no equal element is already contained.

If found, the first equal element is returned, and the hashtable and candidate node are left unchanged. Otherwise, the candidate is inserted using the normal insertion policy, and data is returned. Elements are not freed by this call.

◆ tommy_hashlin_rehash_existing()

TOMMY_API void tommy_hashlin_rehash_existing ( tommy_hashlin *  hashlin,
tommy_hashlin_node *  node,
tommy_hash_t  hash 
)

Updates the hash of an element already contained in the hashtable.

The node must belong to this hashtable. The caller updates the element key and provides its new hash, without modifying tommy_node::index directly. If the hash is unchanged, the node and its position are left unchanged. Otherwise, the node is moved to the tail of the destination bucket, even if the old and new hashes identify the same bucket. The tommy_node::data field and the number of elements are left unchanged. No memory allocation, deallocation or resize is performed. The progressive resize state is left unchanged. Equal keys are allowed; no uniqueness check is performed.

Parameters
hashlinThe hashtable.
nodeThe node whose hash is updated.
hashThe new hash of the element.
Note
This operation is O(1).

◆ tommy_hashlin_foreach()

TOMMY_API void tommy_hashlin_foreach ( tommy_hashlin *  hashlin,
tommy_foreach_func *  func 
)

Calls the specified function for each element in the hashtable.

You cannot add or remove elements from the inside of the callback, but can use it to deallocate them.

tommy_hashlin hashlin;
// initializes the hashtable
tommy_hashlin_init(&hashlin);
...
// creates an element
struct element* elem = malloc(sizeof(struct element));
...
// insert it in the hashtable
tommy_hashlin_insert(&hashlin, &elem->node, elem, tommy_inthash_u32(elem->value));
...
// deallocates all the elements iterating the hashtable
tommy_hashlin_foreach(&hashlin, free);
// deallocates the hashtable
tommy_hashlin_done(&hashlin);

If the callback frees the elements, the hashtable retains dangling node pointers. Call tommy_hashlin_clear() before reusing it, or tommy_hashlin_done() to release its storage.

Parameters
hashlinThe hashtable.
funcFunction to call with each element.

◆ tommy_hashlin_to_list()

TOMMY_API void tommy_hashlin_to_list ( tommy_hashlin *  hashlin,
tommy_list *  list 
)

Transfers all elements from the hashtable into a tommy_list.

Removes every element from the hashlin hashtable and inserts them into the provided list (at the tail), preserving the per-bucket order but not guaranteeing any particular global order. Buckets are visited by increasing active bucket index.

After the call:

  • the hashtable is left in the same state as after tommy_hashlin_init()
  • the target list contains all the elements that were previously in the hashtable

The tommy_node::data and tommy_node::index fields are left unchanged.

This function is useful when you need to:

  • extract all elements to process/sort them outside the hashtable
  • convert the hashtable into a list for sequential iteration
  • prepare for a full clear + re-insertion with different hash/ordering
  • move ownership of the nodes to a list-based container

Typical usage pattern:

tommy_list all_elements;
tommy_list_init(&all_elements);
// move everything out of the hashtable into the list
tommy_hashlin_to_list(&hashlin, &all_elements);
// now you can sort, filter, process sequentially, etc.
tommy_list_sort(&all_elements, compare_by_value);

tommy_list_sort
TOMMY_API void tommy_list_sort(tommy_list *list, tommy_compare_func *cmp)
Sorts a list.
Parameters
hashlinThe hashtable to drain.
listThe destination list. It must be initialized and must not share nodes with the hashtable. Existing elements remain at the head of the list.
Note
This operation is O(b), where b is the number of active buckets before the call.
No new memory is allocated. Additional bucket segments are deallocated.
Any pending resize is canceled. The hashtable and list can be reused immediately.
The relative order of elements that were in the same bucket is preserved, but the order among different buckets is bucket-order dependent.
